meaning.en: Reckless bravery that relies on brawn alone, without judgement or strategy.
meaning.zh: 只凭个人血气之勇，有勇无谋。

examples.zh: 面对强大的对手，光靠匹夫之勇是赢不了的。
examples.en: Against a strong opponent, brute courage alone won't win.

examples.zh: 他不听劝，凭着匹夫之勇冲了上去，结果吃了大亏。
examples.en: He ignored advice, charged in on sheer nerve and came off badly.

story.en: Mencius tells King Xuan that to 'draw the sword, glare and say: how dare he oppose me' is only 匹夫之勇, courage against a single man; true courage is that of a ruler who calms the realm.
story.zh: 《孟子》：“此匹夫之勇，敌一人者也。王请大之！”

usage.en: Derogatory; usually the object of 靠/凭 or a subject in warnings. Not a compliment on courage.
usage.zh: 含贬义，常说“靠/凭匹夫之勇”，多用于告诫。

antonyms: 天下有大勇者，卒然临之而不惊，无故加之而不怒

meaning.en: A beautiful face recalled alongside peach blossom; used for wistful memories of a lost love.
meaning.zh: 指美丽的容颜和盛开的桃花，常用来表达对已逝爱情或旧人的怀念。

equivalents: a face among the peach blossoms
wistful memory of a lost love

examples.zh: 旧地重游，人面桃花，不禁感慨万千。
examples.en: Revisiting the old place, with the face and the blossoms gone, he was overcome with emotion.

examples.zh: 这部电影的名字取自“人面桃花”，讲的是一段错过的爱情。
examples.en: The film's title comes from 'a face among the peach blossoms'; it tells of a love that was missed.

story.en: Cui Hu met a girl by a peach tree one spring; returning a year later he found the house locked and wrote: 'The face and the peach blossom reflected each other red; now the face is gone, the blossoms still smile in the spring breeze.'
story.zh: “去年今日此门中，人面桃花相映红。人面不知何处去，桃花依旧笑春风。”

usage.en: Literary and poetic; often paired with 物是人非. Used for nostalgia, not for describing someone's looks in daily speech.
usage.zh: 文学色彩浓，常与“物是人非”连用，表怀旧伤感。

synonyms: 去年今日此门中，人面桃花相映红
人面不知何处去，桃花依旧笑春风

meaning.en: A person of great prestige and authority in a field, looked up to by all.
meaning.zh: 比喻德高望重或成就卓著、受人敬仰的人。

equivalents: a towering figure in the field

examples.zh: 他是物理学界的泰山北斗，无人不敬。
examples.en: He is a towering figure in physics, respected by all.

examples.zh: 这位老先生是京剧界的泰山北斗。
examples.en: The old gentleman is the doyen of Peking opera.

story.en: The history says that after Han Yu's death, scholars looked up to him like Mount Tai and the Big Dipper.
story.zh: 《新唐书·韩愈传》：“自愈没，其言大行，学者仰之如泰山北斗云。”

usage.en: Praise for a person, often as a noun phrase; formal. Shortened to 泰斗.
usage.zh: 褒义，多作宾语、定语，可简称“泰斗”。

meaning.en: To be all smiles outwardly while harbouring malice and plotting harm.
meaning.zh: 表面和善，内心阴险狠毒。

examples.zh: 他总是笑眯眯的，其实笑里藏刀，千万别得罪他。
examples.en: He's always smiling, but it hides a dagger; don't cross him.

examples.zh: 对这种笑里藏刀的人要多留个心眼。
examples.en: Be on your guard with people who smile while plotting against you.

story.en: The chancellor Li Yifu was gentle and smiling to everyone, yet secretly vicious; people said he had 'a knife inside his smile'.
story.zh: 《旧唐书》说李义府表面温和恭敬，说话时总带微笑，实则阴险，“故时人言义府笑中有刀”。

usage.en: Derogatory; describes a person or manner. Stronger than 口是心非 because real harm is intended.
usage.zh: 贬义，形容人，比“口是心非”更强调暗中害人。

synonyms: 黄鼠狼给鸡拜年——没安好心
黄鼠狼给鸡送礼——不怀好意

meaning.en: A humiliating peace treaty forced on the weaker side when the enemy is at its gates.
meaning.zh: 敌军兵临城下，被迫签订的屈辱性条约。

equivalents: a humiliating peace imposed by force

examples.zh: 战败国只得签订城下之盟，割地赔款。
examples.en: The defeated state had to sign a humiliating treaty and cede land and pay reparations.

examples.zh: 我们宁可谈判受挫，也不愿接受城下之盟。
examples.en: We would rather see talks fail than accept terms dictated at the point of a sword.

usage.en: Formal, used in history and politics; implies disgrace for the side that signs.
usage.zh: 多用于历史、政治语境，含屈辱意味。

story.en: The Zuozhuan tells how Chu besieged Jiao and ambushed its men, then returned having forced Jiao into 'a treaty under the city walls' (为城下之盟). The phrase came to mean a humiliating treaty dictated by an enemy at the gates.
story.zh: 《左传·桓公十二年》载楚伐绞，大败绞人，“为城下之盟而还”。后以“城下之盟”指被迫签订的屈辱和约。

meaning.en: While you go after your prey, a bigger threat is lying in wait for you; often 螳螂捕蝉，黄雀在后.
meaning.zh: 比喻只看到眼前利益，而不知有更大的危险在背后等着。

examples.zh: 他正得意地算计对手，没想到黄雀在后，自己也被人盯上了。
examples.en: Just as he was scheming against his rival, he found someone had him in their sights.

examples.zh: 螳螂捕蝉，黄雀在后，做事要看清全局。
examples.en: The mantis stalks the cicada with the oriole behind it; always see the whole picture.

story.en: A young man warned the King of Wu: a cicada is eyed by a mantis, which is eyed by an oriole, which is eyed by a boy with a slingshot; none sees the danger behind.
story.zh: 少孺子以螳螂捕蝉、黄雀在后、少年持弹丸在下的故事劝谏吴王。

usage.en: Usually a warning, often in full 螳螂捕蝉，黄雀在后; the speaker is the unseen third party.
usage.zh: 多作警示，常与“螳螂捕蝉”连用。

natural: petty skills that save the day

meaning.en: Petty tricks or low-status skills which can nonetheless prove useful in a pinch; also used of petty thieves.
meaning.zh: 指微不足道的技能，或指偷偷摸摸的行为；也指有微末技能的人。

examples.zh: 别小看鸡鸣狗盗之徒，关键时刻他们也能派上用场。
examples.en: Don't look down on people with petty skills; they can prove useful at a crucial moment.

examples.zh: 这种鸡鸣狗盗的勾当，他才不屑去做。
examples.en: He would not stoop to such sneaky, petty dealings.

story.en: Lord Mengchang, held in Qin, escaped thanks to one retainer who stole a fur coat like a dog and another who crowed like a cock to open the pass gate early.
story.zh: 孟尝君被困秦国，门客一人装狗盗得狐白裘，一人学鸡鸣骗开函谷关，得以逃脱。

usage.en: Can be mildly derogatory (petty, underhand) or a wry compliment on odd skills; check context.
usage.zh: 可含贬义，也可指小技能派上大用场，需看语境。

meaning.en: Even if the sea dried up and rocks crumbled; used of a vow or feeling that will never change.
meaning.zh: 即使大海干涸、石头腐烂也不变，形容意志坚定、感情永恒。

examples.zh: 他们发誓海枯石烂，永不分离。
examples.en: They swore never to part, till the seas ran dry.

examples.zh: 海枯石烂，我对祖国的热爱也不会改变。
examples.en: Come what may, my love for my country will never change.

usage.en: Used in vows, often followed by 不变心 or 永不变; mostly about love or loyalty.
usage.zh: 多用于誓言，后常接“不变心”，多指爱情或忠诚。

natural: be wrapped in a horse hide

meaning.en: To die in battle and be brought home wrapped in a horse's hide; the soldier's willingness to give his life for his country.
meaning.zh: 用马皮把尸体包起来，指战死沙场，也形容为国捐躯的决心。

equivalents: lay down one's life in battle

examples.zh: 他立志从军，马革裹尸，在所不惜。
examples.en: He resolved to join the army, ready to die on the battlefield.

examples.zh: 战士们抱着马革裹尸的决心守住了阵地。
examples.en: The soldiers held the position, prepared to die for it.

story.en: General Ma Yuan said a man should die in the wilds of the frontier and be buried wrapped in a horse's hide, not die in bed in the hands of women and children.
story.zh: 马援说：“男儿要当死于边野，以马革裹尸还葬耳，何能卧床上在儿女子手中邪？”

usage.en: Solemn and heroic; used of soldiers and martial resolve, not of ordinary deaths.
usage.zh: 庄重悲壮，用于军人，不用于一般的死亡。

synonyms: 醉卧沙场君莫笑，古来征战几人回

meaning.en: Sweet words on the lips and a sword in the heart: friendly in speech but treacherous in intent.
meaning.zh: 嘴上说得甜蜜，肚子里藏着害人的剑，形容阴险狡诈。

equivalents: honey on the tongue, dagger in the heart

examples.zh: 他对你口蜜腹剑，千万别被他的好话骗了。
examples.en: He's honey-tongued but treacherous; don't be taken in by his flattery.

examples.zh: 历史上的口蜜腹剑之徒，往往最终自食其果。
examples.en: Those who flatter and plot in history usually reap what they sow.

story.en: The Tang chancellor Li Linfu was said to have 'honey in his mouth and a sword in his belly' because he flattered people while secretly ruining them.
story.zh: 时人说李林甫“口有蜜，腹有剑”，表面奉承，暗中陷害。

usage.en: Derogatory; describes a person. Close to 笑里藏刀 but focuses on sweet talk.
usage.zh: 贬义，形容人，与“笑里藏刀”相近，侧重话语甜蜜。

synonyms: 黄鼠狼给鸡送礼——不怀好意
antonyms: 一根肠子通到底——直性子

meaning.en: To study the classics all the way to old age; lifelong devotion to scholarship.
meaning.zh: 直到头发白了还在钻研经典，形容学习刻苦、治学一生。

equivalents: study until one's hair turns white

examples.zh: 他皓首穷经，终于写成这部巨著。
examples.en: Having studied the classics into old age, he finally completed this great work.

examples.zh: 她一生皓首穷经，只为考证一个字的来历。
examples.en: She spent her whole life poring over the classics to trace the origin of a single character.

usage.en: Praise for diligence, but can also hint at pedantry. Literary; often about scholars of old.
usage.zh: 多含赞赏，有时带书呆子意味；书面语。

meaning.en: Soft, sentimental or decadent music that saps the will; by extension, any frivolous, unwholesome art.
meaning.zh: 柔弱颓废、使人萎靡的乐曲，也泛指低级庸俗的文艺。

examples.zh: 他认为这些歌曲都是靡靡之音，不值得听。
examples.en: He thinks these songs are decadent drivel not worth hearing.

examples.zh: 在乱世里，靡靡之音往往更容易流行。
examples.en: In troubled times, decadent music tends to become popular.

usage.en: Disapproving; a term of moral judgement. Pronounced mǐ mǐ, not mí mí.
usage.zh: 贬义，带道德评判；读 mǐ mǐ。

story.en: The Annals of Yin record that King Zhou had his musician compose 'new licentious sounds, northern-village dances and decadent music' (靡靡之乐). The later idiom 靡靡之音 for soft, enervating music derives from this.
story.zh: 《史记·殷本纪》载商纣王“使师涓作新淫声，北里之舞，靡靡之乐”；后世“靡靡之音”即由此而来，指萎靡颓废的音乐。

meaning.en: A marriage between two families, from the intermarriage of the states of Qin and Jin.
meaning.zh: 指两家联姻，结为亲家。

equivalents: the bond of two families by marriage

examples.zh: 两家结为秦晋之好，亲上加亲。
examples.en: The two families were united by marriage, becoming even closer.

examples.zh: 祝愿二位喜结秦晋之好，白头偕老。
examples.en: We wish the two of you a happy union and a lifetime together.

usage.en: Auspicious, formal; used in wedding congratulations and about families, not individuals.
usage.zh: 喜庆用语，多用于婚礼祝贺，指两家联姻。

story.en: The states of Qin and Jin intermarried over generations in the Spring and Autumn period, notably when Duke Mu of Qin gave daughters to Prince Chong'er of Jin (Zuozhuan, 23rd year of Duke Xi). The idiom for a marriage alliance comes from this history.
story.zh: 春秋时秦、晋两国世代联姻，《左传·僖公二十三年》载秦穆公以女嫁晋公子重耳；后遂以“秦晋之好”称两家结为婚姻。

meaning.en: Night falling and the road at an end: a person or cause reduced to desperate straits.
meaning.zh: 天快黑了，路也走到尽头，比喻处境艰难、末日临近。

equivalents: at the end of one's rope

examples.zh: 这家公司已是日暮途穷，难逃倒闭的命运。
examples.en: The company is at the end of its rope and cannot escape bankruptcy.

examples.zh: 他自知日暮途穷，只好选择投降。
examples.en: Knowing he was finished, he had no choice but to surrender.

story.en: Wu Zixu said that with the sun setting and the road still long, he was acting against normal order out of urgency.
story.zh: 伍子胥说：“吾日莫途远，吾故倒行而逆施之。”

usage.en: Used of people, groups and causes in decline; literary. Original form 日暮途远 is less common now.
usage.zh: 多指人或事业走投无路，书面语；原形“日暮途远”今较少用。

antonyms: 天戴其苍，地履其黄；纵有千古，横有八荒；前途似海，来日方长

natural: a fine match for a gentleman

meaning.en: A gentleman's fitting partner; originally the poem's line saying the lovely maiden is a good match for a gentleman.
meaning.zh: 君子的好配偶，常指男子追求心仪的女子。

equivalents: a fitting match for a gentleman

examples.zh: 他读到《关雎》，深感“窈窕淑女，君子好逑”写尽了少年心事。
examples.en: Reading Guan Ju, he felt the line “the fair maiden, a fine match for the gentleman” captured the whole of youthful longing.

examples.zh: 他对她一见钟情，决意君子好逑。
examples.en: He fell for her at first sight and resolved to court her properly.

story.en: The first poem of the Book of Songs: 'The fair and gentle maiden is a fine mate for a gentleman'.
story.zh: 《关雎》：“关关雎鸠，在河之洲。窈窕淑女，君子好逑。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Literary; usually quoted with 窈窕淑女. Here 逑 means 'mate', and 好 is read hǎo.
usage.zh: 书面语，常与“窈窕淑女”连用；“逑”意为配偶。

meaning.en: An army fighting in grief and righteous anger is sure to win.
meaning.zh: 受压迫、怀着悲愤的军队士气高昂，一定能打胜仗。

examples.zh: 球队被误判后哀兵必胜，下半场连进三球。
examples.en: After the wrongful call the team fought back with a vengeance and scored three in the second half.

examples.zh: 人们说哀兵必胜，这支受委屈的队伍反而更团结。
examples.en: As they say, the wronged fight hardest; the slighted team grew closer.

story.en: Laozi: when two armies of equal strength meet, the one that grieves wins (抗兵相加，哀者胜矣).

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前6—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 6th–4th c. BC

usage.en: Often used of sport and competition after a setback; the side must be the 'wronged' one.
usage.zh: 常用于体育、竞争中受挫一方，须是受委屈的一方。

meaning.en: Food given with contempt or insult; accepting it means losing one's dignity.
meaning.zh: 带着侮辱、轻视意味施舍的食物，也泛指不尊重人的施舍。

examples.zh: 他饿死也不吃嗟来之食。
examples.en: He would rather starve than accept a handout offered with scorn.

examples.zh: 尊严比什么都重要，嗟来之食我不要。
examples.en: Dignity matters most; I won't take charity thrown at me.

story.en: In a famine a rich man offered food with a rude 'Hey, come and eat!'; Qian Ao refused it and starved to death.
story.zh: 黔敖在饥荒中施食，叫：“嗟，来食！”饥民扬目而视曰：“予唯不食嗟来之食，以至于斯也。”

usage.en: Often with 不食/不受; shows self-respect. 嗟 is jiē, an interjection.
usage.zh: 常说“不食嗟来之食”，表现有骨气；“嗟”是叹词，读 jiē。

natural: one day of sun, ten of cold

meaning.en: Working at something for a day and then neglecting it for ten; lacking perseverance.
meaning.zh: 晒一天，冷十天，比喻做事缺乏恒心，时断时续。

examples.zh: 学外语不能一曝十寒，要天天坚持。
examples.en: You can't learn a language by fits and starts; practise daily.

examples.zh: 他的健身计划一曝十寒，三个月毫无效果。
examples.en: His workout plan was on and off, so three months brought no results.

story.en: Mencius: even the easiest-growing plant will not live if you give it one day of sun and then ten days of cold.
story.zh: 孟子：“虽有天下易生之物也，一日暴之，十日寒之，未有能生者也。”

usage.en: Criticism of lack of persistence. 曝 is read pù here; also written 一暴十寒.
usage.zh: 批评缺乏恒心；“曝”此处读 pù，也作“一暴十寒”。

antonyms: 铁杵磨绣针——非一日之功
锲而舍之，朽木不折；锲而不舍，金石可镂

natural: bore a hole to borrow light

meaning.en: To bore a hole in the wall to steal a neighbour's candlelight for reading; studying hard despite poverty.
meaning.zh: 在墙上凿洞借邻居的烛光读书，形容家贫而刻苦读书。

examples.zh: 他凿壁偷光的故事激励了一代代读书人。
examples.en: His story of reading by borrowed light has inspired generations of students.

examples.zh: 条件再差也要像古人凿壁偷光那样坚持学习。
examples.en: However poor the conditions, keep studying as the ancients did by bored-through light.

story.en: Kuang Heng was too poor to buy candles; he cut a hole in the wall to let in his neighbour's light and read by it.
story.zh: 匡衡勤学而无烛，邻舍有烛而不逮，衡乃穿壁引其光，以书映光而读之。

usage.en: Praise for diligence under hardship; often paired with 悬梁刺股.
usage.zh: 褒义，赞扬艰苦中勤学，常与“悬梁刺股”并用。

natural: the friendship of Guan and Bao

meaning.en: A deep, trusting friendship, like that of Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya of the Spring and Autumn period.
meaning.zh: 像管仲和鲍叔牙那样互相了解、彼此信任的深厚友谊。

equivalents: friends who truly know each other

examples.zh: 他们俩是管鲍之交，几十年不离不弃。
examples.en: The two are true bosom friends, who have stood by each other for decades.

examples.zh: 管鲍之交不是靠利益维系的，而是靠相知。
examples.en: A friendship like Guan and Bao's rests on understanding, not on profit.

story.en: Bao Shuya knew Guan Zhong's character, never blamed him for taking more of the profit when they traded together, and later recommended him as chief minister of Qi.
story.zh: 管仲说：“生我者父母，知我者鲍子也。”

usage.en: Praise for friendship; formal. Often with 堪称/可谓.
usage.zh: 褒义，用于友情，较正式，常说“堪称管鲍之交”。

meaning.en: A natural feeling of compassion for another's suffering.
meaning.zh: 对别人的不幸表示同情、不忍之心。

examples.zh: 看到流浪的小狗，他心生恻隐之心。
examples.en: Seeing the stray puppy, he was filled with compassion.

examples.zh: 再冷酷的人也有恻隐之心。
examples.en: Even the coldest people have some compassion.

story.en: Mencius: seeing a child about to fall into a well, anyone would feel alarm and compassion; the heart of compassion is the beginning of humaneness.
story.zh: 孟子：“恻隐之心，仁之端也。”

usage.en: Positive; usually with 有/动/生. 恻 is cè; 隐 is yǐn.
usage.zh: 褒义，常与“有、动、生”搭配。

meaning.en: A group of bad companions or villains who band together.
meaning.zh: 比喻勾结在一起的坏人。

examples.zh: 他整天和一帮狐群狗党混在一起，不务正业。
examples.en: He hangs about with a gang of rogues all day and does no honest work.

examples.zh: 警方端掉了这个狐群狗党的窝点。
examples.en: The police raided the gang's hideout.

usage.en: Derogatory; refers to a group of people.
usage.zh: 贬义，指一伙坏人。

meaning.en: To be left speechless, mouth open and tongue tied, from fear, shock or having no answer.
meaning.zh: 张着嘴说不出话来，形容理屈词穷或吓呆了的样子。

examples.zh: 被老师当场点名，他张口结舌，答不上来。
examples.en: Called on by the teacher, he was tongue-tied and could not answer.

examples.zh: 面对记者的追问，发言人张口结舌。
examples.en: Pressed by reporters, the spokesman was lost for words.

usage.en: Used for people at a loss; often 张口结舌地…. Not for deliberate silence.
usage.zh: 形容一时语塞，不用于故意沉默。

meaning.en: A promise that is settled with a single word: said to confirm an agreement.
meaning.zh: 一句话就决定了，表示说话算数，不再改变。

examples.zh: 明天八点见，一言为定！
examples.en: See you at eight tomorrow, agreed!

examples.zh: 咱们一言为定，谁也不许反悔。
examples.en: It's a deal; neither of us may go back on it.

usage.en: Typically said to close an agreement; casual, often with 就这么/咱们. Often follows with 驷马难追.
usage.zh: 常用于达成约定时，口语，后可接“驷马难追”。

meaning.en: Cruel and ungrateful, with the heart of a wolf and the lungs of a dog.
meaning.zh: 心肠像狼和狗一样狠毒，形容人忘恩负义、没有良心。

examples.zh: 他对救命恩人都下得了手，真是狼心狗肺。
examples.en: He could harm even the man who saved his life; he is utterly heartless.

examples.zh: 你这个狼心狗肺的东西，我白养你了！
examples.en: You ungrateful wretch; I raised you for nothing!

usage.en: Strong insult, used in anger; avoid in polite speech.
usage.zh: 骂人话，语气重，礼貌场合避免。
